extracted.intended_audience: administrators, Title IX coordinators, legal/compliance officers, and policymakers at recipient educational institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and recipient obligations under final Title IX regulations addressing pregnancy and related conditions, including voluntary separate programs, leaves of absence, reasonable modifications, determinations of medically necessary leave, lactation space, and interactions with other federal requirements (e.g., Title IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary participation in separate programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may allow a student who is pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions to participate voluntarily in a separate portion of the recipient's education program or activity; such participation must be completely voluntary on the part of the student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must not coerce or pressure any student to participate in a separate program. The Department clarifies that 'voluntarily' means recipients may neither coerce nor pressure students into such programs; this longstanding rule dates to the original 1975 regulations and OCR guidance (1991, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability standard for separate programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate programs for pregnant students must be 'comparable' to those offered to students who are not pregnant and do not have related conditions—i.e., of equivalent quality or similar such that they are capable of comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparability refers to all aspects of a student's access to educational opportunity. The Department interprets 'comparable' to mean educational quality and academic offerings similar to the regular program; an alternative program that provides only a vocational track with no advanced academic or college-preparatory classes would not meet the standard. The Department declined to adopt 'substantially equal' as a higher standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for assessing comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a separate portion is 'comparable,' the Department considers factors as appropriate, including policies and criteria of admission; educational benefits (quality, range, content of curriculum and services); quality and availability of books, instructional materials, and technology; qualifications of instructors; and quality, accessibility, and availability of facilities and resources provided to the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These §106.34(b)(3)-type factors are helpful but not a fixed checklist; determinations depend on facts and circumstances. Supplemental courses or services tailored to pregnant students (e.g., parenting classes) may be permissible when overall comparability is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of different program forms when comparable
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary programs that differ in form (e.g., online instruction or supplemental parenting courses) may still be 'comparable' if they provide equivalent access to educational opportunity given the student's needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: online options that permit a student on bed rest to remain engaged can be comparable even if they lack certain extracurricular elements; programs that include parenting classes may exceed general curriculum offerings but still meet comparability. The Department warns that shifting to a 'substantially equal' standard could incorrectly render such permissible programs impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary leave of absence for pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must allow a student to take a voluntary leave of absence related to pregnancy or related conditions for, at minimum, the period deemed medically necessary by the student's healthcare provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave must be voluntary on the student's part; the medically necessary period is a minimum requirement. Recipients must permit leave for admitted students (including before classes start) and may not require withdrawal and reapplication for such students. The Department preserved this obligation since it is critical to ensuring equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement and make-up opportunity after leave
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must reinstate a student to the academic status the student held when voluntary leave began and must provide a meaningful opportunity and reasonable time to make up missed coursework and exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a presumption that students returning from leave should be reinstated to the same extracurricular status, but limited instances may make exact reinstatement administratively impracticable. Recipients may offer alternatives to making up missed work, particularly after longer leaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'student' and application before classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX definition of 'student' includes anyone admitted to a recipient institution, so admitted students who need pregnancy-related leave before the start of classes qualify for voluntary leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not enforce a general policy requiring students who need pre-term or early-term leave to withdraw and reapply; those policies must exempt students needing pregnancy-related leave in order to comply with §106.40(b)(3)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with recipient leave policies and reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student qualifies for a longer leave under a recipient's existing student leave policy than the medically necessary period, the recipient must permit the student to take leave under that policy; requests for additional time beyond available policy leave should be considered under the reasonable modification standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must determine whether additional time beyond the medically necessary period is a reasonable modification under §106.40(b)(3)(ii). Reasonable modifications are individualized and distinct from the guaranteed minimum medically necessary leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fundamental alteration defense to providing voluntary leave
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's belief that providing leave and reinstatement would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program or activity does not excuse the obligation to allow a voluntary leave of absence and reinstatement for pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 1975 recipients have been required to allow voluntary leave for pregnancy-related conditions and reinstate students; §106.40(b)(3)(iv) requires offering such leave irrespective of a recipient's fundamental-alteration concerns. Implementation discretion remains, but must be consistent with Title IX and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of medically necessary leave by licensed healthcare provider
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensed healthcare provider may verify that a leave is medically necessary; 'licensed' broadly encompasses any healthcare professional qualified to practice in their State and need not be limited to physicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes advanced practice clinicians (e.g., nurse practitioners, midwives, doulas, registered nurses, lactation consultants). Recipients are not required to verify licensure across States or understand varying licensure systems; the provision intentionally avoids onerous technical licensure verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Title IV (federal student aid) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX-required voluntary leave of absence does not automatically mandate a Title IV withdrawal for financial aid purposes; if a leave qualifies as an 'approved leave of absence' under 34 CFR 668.22(d)(1), it is a temporary interruption and not a withdrawal for Title IV calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must apply Title IV rules to determine whether a leave is an approved leave for financial aid purposes; if combined approved leaves exceed 180 days in a 12-month period, Title IV 'return to Title IV' calculations and other requirements apply. Title IX obligations do not authorize Title IV actions that disadvantage students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and reasonable modifications obligation (§106.40(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have a distinct obligation to consult with students and offer and implement reasonable modifications that meet individualized needs to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access when pregnancy or related conditions require accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable modifications must be considered across all parts of an education program or activity, including professional degree programs and licensure-subject programs. The reasonable modification inquiry (including fundamental alteration and undue burden) is fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide a private, clean, usable lactation space and breaks for a student who is lactating; the space must be usable for both breastfeeding and pumping and should not be a bathroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of lactation space can impair health, interrupt learning, and force students into inappropriate places (cars, janitor closets, bathroom stalls). The Department ties the requirement to public health benefits and consistency with other federal and state laws (ACA, FLSA) and administrative/court precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space amenities, location, and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended lactation spaces include amenities (chair, flat surface, electrical outlet, running water, refrigerator/cooler), be in reasonable proximity to students' places of study, be available during evenings/weekends, and be administered to accommodate multiple users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department was asked to clarify required number/location of spaces, whether new construction is required, and how shared use is managed. Small schools raised concerns about space constraints and sought flexibility. The rule contemplates practical implementation consistent with accessibility and non-discrimination obligations; specifics may depend on recipient size and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breastfeeding/expressing milk in non-designated locations and K–12 nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters recommended affirming a student's right to express milk or breastfeed in places other than a designated lactation space (e.g., offices, childcare facilities, public spaces) consistent with State/local laws; commenters also sought clarification about elementary/secondary settings and onsite childcare contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues raised include whether and how students in K–12 can breastfeed in lactation spaces and how onsite childcare affects access; the Department acknowledged state/local law intersections and practical differences across educational levels, viewing these as fact-specific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of parenting students and sex-stereotype protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department acknowledged comments urging extension of §106.40(b)(1) to apply to parenting students and reiterated that treating parenting students differently based on sex is prohibited under §106.40(a) and that discrimination based on sex stereotypes is prohibited under §106.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will consider the need for revisions to explicitly cover parenting students in future rulemakings, balancing benefits with potential costs and administrative burdens on recipients.
